name: Magileads
description: Magileads is a B2B prospecting and multichannel outreach platform for lead generation, contact management, and PRM workflows.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Magileads API key sent in the X-API-Key header for every request.
authentication.notes: Generate an API key in Magileads, then paste it here. The app sends that key in the X-API-Key header on every request.

setupGuide.title: Connect Magileads
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Magileads API key from a workspace that can access the lists, PRM, tags, and blacklist resources you want to manage.

steps.title: Open Magileads
steps.description: Sign in to the Magileads workspace that owns the data you want MindCloud to manage.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key
steps.description: Open the Magileads API settings and copy an active API key for that workspace.

steps.title: Paste the API key here
steps.description: Store the key in the MindCloud connection as the single `API Key` secret.

steps.title: Verify the key can reach your data
steps.description: Confirm the same key can list your contact lists or PRM resources before saving the connection.

name: MailBluster
description: Manage MailBluster email marketing resources including leads, custom fields, products, orders, and ecommerce activity through the MailBluster API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a MailBluster brand API key. MailBluster accepts the raw key in the Authorization header on each API request.
authentication.notes: MailBluster documents the API key as a raw Authorization header value, not a Bearer token. The REST API headers override the generic bearer default with Authorization: {{credentials.apiKey}}.

setupGuide.title: How to create a MailBluster API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a MailBluster brand where you can open brand settings.

steps.title: Open your brand settings
steps.description: Sign in to MailBluster, choose the brand you want to connect, then open Brand Settings.

steps.title: Open the API keys tab
steps.description: In Settings, open the API keys tab.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Select Create new, enter a name that helps you recognize how the key will be used, then create the key.

steps.title: Paste the API key
steps.description: Copy the API key value from MailBluster and paste it into the API Key field for this connection.

name: MailboxValidator
description: Validate email addresses and detect disposable or free providers

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use your MailboxValidator API key.

setupGuide.title: Set up your MailboxValidator API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a MailboxValidator account with an active API plan.

steps.title: Choose a MailboxValidator API plan
steps.description: Open the MailboxValidator API plans page and subscribe to the API plan you want to use. MailboxValidator states that API keys are provided when you sign up for an API plan.

steps.title: Sign in and retrieve your API key
steps.description: Sign in to MailboxValidator, then open your dashboard and copy the API key for your API plan. The single-email validation docs state that you retrieve the key from your dashboard.

steps.title: Paste the API key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MailboxValidator connection in MindCloud and paste the API key into the API Key field.

name: Mailcheck
description: Verify email deliverability, run bulk email checks, analyze email authenticity, rotate MailCheck API keys, and inspect MailCheck account usage from the MailCheck API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: MailCheck secret API key used as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
authentication.notes: Use your MailCheck secret API key (`sk_live_...`). This is a server-side credential and should not be exposed in browser code.

setupGuide.title: Create a MailCheck API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: MailCheck secret keys start with `sk_live_` and must be kept private.

steps.title: Open the MailCheck dashboard
steps.description: Sign in to MailCheck and open the API Keys page from the dashboard.

steps.title: Create or copy a secret key
steps.description: Generate a new secret API key if needed, or copy an existing active key that starts with `sk_live_`.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud Mailcheck connection form and paste the key into the API key field.

name: Mailchimp
description: Manage audiences, create campaigns, automate emails, and track engagement.

authentication.name: OAuth 2
authentication.description: OAuth 2 authentication for accessing Mailchimp Marketing API data on behalf of users.

credentials.name: Server Prefix
credentials.description: Mailchimp data center prefix used in API base URL (for example: us19).

setupGuide.title: Connect Mailchimp OAuth 2
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Use a Mailchimp account that can register OAuth apps and prepare the redirect URI used by your MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Register your app in Mailchimp
steps.description: In Mailchimp, open Registered Apps and create a new app for this integration.

steps.title: Copy client_id and client_secret
steps.description: After creating the app, copy the client_id and client_secret values from the Mailchimp app page.

steps.title: Find your server prefix
steps.description: Enter your Mailchimp data center prefix (for example us19). You can find it in your Mailchimp URL or API key suffix (-us19).

steps.title: Set the redirect URI in Mailchimp
steps.description: Configure the redirect URI in your Mailchimp app settings to match the URI shown in MindCloud before connecting.

steps.title: Authorize access
steps.description: Click Connect in MindCloud and approve access on Mailchimp’s OAuth consent screen.

steps.title: Copy the token immediately

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud

setupGuide.title: Set up your MariaDB connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the MariaDB host name, database name, username, and password for the database account MindCloud should use. If you are connecting to a remote MariaDB server, make sure the server allows remote client access.

steps.title: Collect the connection details from your MariaDB administrator or hosting provider
steps.description: Get the host, database name, username, and password for the MariaDB database you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Choose the port
steps.description: Use the MariaDB TCP port for the server. If your administrator did not specify a custom port, use the MariaDB default port 3306.

steps.title: Enter the connection fields in MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud MariaDB connection form, enter the Host, Port, Database, User, and Password values exactly as provided for the MariaDB account.

name: Mediastack
description: Access worldwide live and historical news articles and news-source metadata from Mediastack's REST API.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate Mediastack requests with the account API access key sent as the access_key query parameter.
authentication.notes: Mediastack uses a query-string API key named access_key. The MindCloud connection stores the key as credentials.apiKey; API-level request mapping sends it as access_key={{credentials.apiKey}}.

setupGuide.title: Connect Mediastack
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Mediastack account and the API access key from your account dashboard.

steps.title: Open your Mediastack dashboard

steps.title: Copy the API access key
steps.description: Copy the unique API access key shown for your account. Mediastack documents this key as the value used for the access_key request parameter.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to this connection setup screen and paste the copied key into the API key field.

name: Meegle
description: Meegle integration for MindCloud using Meegle OpenAPI with custom token-based authentication.

authentication.name: Meegle Custom Auth
authentication.description: Custom Meegle plugin-token authentication using Plugin ID, Plugin Secret, and User Key.

credentials.name: Plugin Secret

credentials.name: User Key
credentials.description: Meegle user_key for user-scoped request flows when required.

setupGuide.title: How to set up your Meegle connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Meegle plugin, its Plugin ID and Plugin Secret, and a User Key from the Meegle account that can access the target space.

steps.title: Open your Meegle plugin
steps.description: In Meegle Developer Platform, open the plugin you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Copy the Plugin ID and Plugin Secret
steps.description: From the Basic Information page, copy the Plugin ID and Plugin Secret into the MindCloud connection fields.

steps.title: Copy the User Key for the target account
steps.description: Open the Meegle space you want to query and copy the User Key for the account that should scope requests.

steps.title: Authenticate the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste Plugin ID, Plugin Secret, and User Key into the Meegle connection, then save or authenticate the connection.

name: Megaapi Start
description: Send WhatsApp messages, manage instances, webhooks, chats, and groups

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Bearer token authentication with tenant host and instance key.

credentials.name: Host
credentials.description: MegaAPI tenant host shown in the instance details.

credentials.name: Instance Key
credentials.description: Instance key used in MegaAPI request paths.

setupGuide.title: Connect your MegaAPI Start account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need an active MegaAPI Start instance. Keep the instance details page open so you can copy the Host, Token, and Instance Key.

steps.title: Sign in to the MegaAPI panel
steps.description: Open the MegaAPI Start login page and sign in with the account that owns the instance you want to connect.

steps.title: Open the instance details
steps.description: In the panel, open the target instance and click Detalhes. MegaAPI documents that the instance details screen shows the host, token, and instance key for that instance.

steps.title: Copy the Host value
steps.description: Copy the Host exactly as shown in the instance details. It should look similar to apistart01.megaapi.com.br.

steps.title: Copy the Token value
steps.description: Copy the Token from the same details screen. MindCloud stores this value as the API Key and sends it as a Bearer token on each request.

steps.title: Copy the Instance Key value
steps.description: Copy the Instance Key exactly as shown in the instance details screen.

actions.name: Get Connection Status
actions.description: Retrieves WhatsApp connection status from Megaapi Start.

setupGuide.title: Create a Meisterplan API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Meisterplan account with the "Access Meisterplan APIs and Connect External Applications" permission.

steps.title: Sign in to Meisterplan
steps.description: Open your Meisterplan system and sign in with the account you want to connect.

steps.title: Open the API token page
steps.description: Open your user profile, click Manage Apps, then select API Tokens.

steps.title: Create a token
steps.description: Click Add API Token, enter a name, and create the token.

steps.title: Copy the token
steps.description: Copy the API token and store it somewhere safe. Meisterplan only shows the token value when you create it.

steps.title: Paste the token into MindCloud
steps.description: When you create the MindCloud connection, paste the copied value into the API Token field.

name: Mekari Qontak
description: Qontak CRM wrapper for Mekari's HMAC-signed CRM API surface.

authentication.name: HMAC
authentication.description: HMAC-signed credentials for the Mekari Qontak CRM API.
authentication.notes: Qontak CRM requests require HMAC-signed Authorization and Date headers and the X-Crm-User-Sso-Id header. Credential scope must include the target CRM endpoints.

credentials.name: Client ID
credentials.description: Mekari HMAC client ID for the Qontak CRM application.

credentials.name: Client Secret
credentials.description: Mekari HMAC client secret for the Qontak CRM application.

credentials.name: CRM User SSO ID
credentials.description: Qontak CRM user SSO ID sent in the X-Crm-User-Sso-Id header for requests.

setupGuide.title: Set up Mekari Qontak CRM credentials
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You must have access to Mekari Developer and Qontak CRM for the same company. HMAC credentials are scoped to one company and one product.

steps.title: Create or open a Mekari Developer application
steps.description: Sign in to Mekari Developer, open Applications, and select only the Qontak CRM scopes required for your integration.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
steps.description: Keep both values private. They are required to generate the HMAC Authorization header for every request.

steps.title: Provide the CRM user SSO ID used for actions
steps.description: Qontak CRM requests require the X-Crm-User-Sso-Id header for the user whose actions will run through the wrapper.

name: Mendeley
description: Reference manager and academic collaboration platform for managing research libraries, documents, profiles, groups, and annotations through the Mendeley API.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Connect a Mendeley developer application using OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow.
authentication.notes: Use a Mendeley developer application configured for Authorization Code flow. The application ID is the client_id, the app secret is the client_secret, and the registered redirect URI must match the MindCloud callback exactly.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Mendeley account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Mendeley/Elsevier account and access to the Mendeley Developer Portal so you can register an application.

steps.title: Open the Mendeley Developer Portal
steps.description: Sign in to the Mendeley Developer Portal so you can manage your API application.

steps.title: Create or open your application
steps.description: Create a Mendeley application if you do not already have one, or open an existing application you want to use with MindCloud.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL
steps.description: Make sure the application redirect URL is exactly `https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/mendeley/callback`.

steps.title: Copy your application credentials
steps.description: Copy the Application ID and Application Secret from your Mendeley application settings. In MindCloud, use the Application ID as the Client ID and the Application Secret as the Client Secret.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, enter the Client ID and Client Secret, then continue through the OAuth window and approve access.

steps.title: Create a personal access token

steps.title: Store the token in this connection

The participant's contact information. For more information on identifier keys and values, please refer to the "Conversation Participants" page.

setupGuide.title: Set up your Microsoft 365 connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Microsoft Entra admin center for the tenant you want to connect and permission to create or manage an app registration.

steps.title: Create an app registration in Microsoft Entra
steps.description: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a new app registration for this MindCloud connection. Use a clear name your team will recognize.

steps.title: Copy the Application (client) ID
steps.description: On the Overview page for the new app registration, copy the Application (client) ID. You will paste this into MindCloud as the client ID.

steps.title: Add the MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: Open the Authentication page for the app registration, add a Web platform if needed, and add this redirect URI exactly: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/microsoft365/callback

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.description: Open Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret, and copy the secret Value immediately. Microsoft only shows the Value once.

steps.title: Paste the client ID and client secret into MindCloud and connect
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, enter the Application (client) ID and the client secret Value, then start the Microsoft sign-in flow.

name: Microsoft 365 Excel
description: Access Microsoft 365 Excel workbook files through Microsoft Graph, including OneDrive-backed workbook, worksheet, and range operations.

authentication.name: Microsoft Entra OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect to Microsoft 365 Excel through Microsoft Graph using a Microsoft Entra OAuth 2.0 app registration.
authentication.notes: Use redirect URI `https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/microsoft365Excel/callback`. Required delegated Microsoft Graph scopes: `User.Read Files.ReadWrite offline_access openid profile`. Tenant admins may need to grant consent for Files.ReadWrite.

setupGuide.title: Set up your Microsoft 365 Excel connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Microsoft Entra admin center for the tenant you want to connect and permission to create or manage an app registration.

steps.title: Create an app registration in Microsoft Entra
steps.description: Create a new app registration for this MindCloud Excel connection. Use a clear name your team will recognize.

steps.title: Copy the Application (client) ID
steps.description: On the Overview page, copy the Application (client) ID. You will use it as the OAuth client ID.

steps.title: Add the MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: Open Authentication for the app registration, add a Web platform if needed, and add this redirect URI exactly: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/microsoft365Excel/callback

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.description: Create a new client secret and copy the secret Value immediately. Microsoft only shows the Value once.

steps.title: Confirm Graph delegated permissions
steps.description: Make sure the app registration can request delegated Microsoft Graph permissions for User.Read, Files.ReadWrite, offline_access, openid, and profile.

steps.title: Paste the client ID and client secret into MindCloud and connect
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, enter the Application (client) ID and client secret Value, then start the Microsoft sign-in flow.

name: Microsoft Intune
description: Manage Microsoft Intune device, app, configuration, and policy resources through Microsoft Graph.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Connect to Microsoft Intune through Microsoft Graph using the Microsoft identity platform authorization-code flow.

setupGuide.title: Set up your Microsoft Intune connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Microsoft Entra admin center for the tenant you want to connect, permission to create or manage an app registration, and an active Intune license for that tenant.

steps.title: Create or open an app registration in Microsoft Entra
steps.description: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, create a new app registration or open the app registration you want to use for this MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Add the MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: Open Authentication, add a Web platform if needed, and add this redirect URI exactly: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/microsoftIntune/callback

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.description: Open Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret, and copy the secret Value immediately. Microsoft only shows the Value once.

steps.title: Add Microsoft Graph API permissions
steps.description: Add delegated Microsoft Graph permissions for User.Read, DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All, DeviceManagementApps.Read.All, and DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All. Grant admin consent if your tenant requires it.

steps.title: Paste the client ID and client secret into MindCloud and connect
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, enter the Application (client) ID and client secret Value, then start the Microsoft sign-in flow.

actions.name: Get My Profile
actions.description: Retrieves the signed-in user profile from Microsoft Intune.

name: Microsoft Power BI
description: Manage Power BI workspaces, reports, dashboards, datasets, and dataflows

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect Power BI with Microsoft Entra delegated OAuth2.

setupGuide.title: Set up Microsoft Power BI OAuth
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a work or school Microsoft account that can open the Power BI service and permission to register an app in Microsoft Entra.

steps.title: Confirm you can open the Power BI service
steps.description: Sign in to Power BI in a browser with your work or school account. If self-service is enabled, Microsoft can assign the initial license the first time you open the service.

steps.title: Register a Microsoft Entra app
steps.description: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open App registrations and create a new app registration for this Power BI connection.

steps.title: Add your redirect URI
steps.description: Open the app registration authentication settings and add the web redirect URI that MindCloud shows for this connection.

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.description: Open Certificates & secrets in the app registration and create a new client secret. Copy the secret value now because Microsoft shows it only once.

steps.title: Grant Power BI delegated permissions
steps.description: Add the delegated Power BI API permissions required for the actions you want to use, then grant admin consent if your tenant requires it.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Connect with a Microsoft work or school account to access SharePoint through Microsoft Graph.
authentication.notes: Use a Microsoft 365 work or school account with access to the target SharePoint sites. Tenant admin consent may be required for the configured Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
authentication.scopes: offline_access User.Read Sites.Read.All Sites.ReadWrite.All Files.Read.All Files.ReadWrite.All

setupGuide.title: Connect Microsoft SharePoint
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Microsoft 365 work or school tenant and permission to create or edit a Microsoft Entra app registration. Personal Microsoft accounts are not enough for the SharePoint APIs used in this connector.

steps.title: Register or reuse a Microsoft Entra application
steps.description: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open App registrations and create a new application, or reuse an existing MindCloud application if your team already manages one.

steps.title: Choose organization-only sign-in
steps.description: Under Supported account types, choose Accounts in any organizational directory. Do not choose an option that includes personal Microsoft accounts for this SharePoint connector.

steps.title: Add the MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: Open Authentication, add a Web platform, and register this redirect URI: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/microsoftSharePoint/callback

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.description: Open Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret, and copy the secret Value immediately. Microsoft only shows the value once.

steps.title: Add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions
steps.description: Open API permissions, add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions, and include offline_access, Files.Read.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.Read.All, and Sites.ReadWrite.All. Grant admin consent if your tenant requires it.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Provide the Application (client) ID and client secret value to the MindCloud team so the app-level OAuth settings can be completed, then sign in with a work or school account that already has access to the target SharePoint sites.

steps.description: Create a client secret and copy the value immediately. Use the client ID and client secret when creating the MindCloud connection.

steps.description: Add delegated permissions for the selected action set: User.Read, Team.ReadBasic.All, TeamMember.Read.All, Channel.ReadBasic.All, ChannelSettings.ReadWrite.All, Channel.Create, ChannelMember.Read.All, Files.Read.All, TeamsTab.Read.All, TeamsAppInstallation.ReadForTeam, ChannelMessage.Read.All, ChannelMessage.Send, Chat.ReadWrite, ChatMessage.Send, Chat.Create, and TeamsAppInstallation.ReadForChat. Request offline_access in the OAuth scope string so MindCloud can receive refresh tokens.

steps.title: Grant tenant consent when required
steps.description: If your organization requires administrator approval for these delegated permissions, grant admin consent before testing the MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Connect from MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, enter the client ID and client secret, and complete OAuth sign-in with a work or school account that can access the target Teams tenant.

setupGuide.title: Connect Mifiel with App ID and App Secret
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Mifiel account with the Integrations functionality contracted and active, plus available document credits.

steps.title: Open the Mifiel Access Tokens page
steps.description: Sign in to Mifiel and open the page where your production App ID and App Secret are managed.

steps.title: Generate or copy your production credentials
steps.description: Mifiel says sandbox access tokens do not work in production. Generate new production access tokens if needed and save the App Secret immediately because Mifiel says you will not be able to view it again.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud connection form, paste the Mifiel App ID into the Username field and the App Secret into the Password field.

steps.title: Open the Developer section in Mihu
steps.description: Sign in to your Mihu workspace, click your profile icon in the top-right corner, and open `Developer` from the menu.

steps.title: Create an API token
steps.description: Create a new API token, give it a descriptive name, and copy the token immediately after it is generated.

steps.title: Fill the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Paste your workspace subdomain into `Workspace Subdomain` and paste your token into the API key field.

name: MILKEE
description: REST API integration for MILKEE, a Swiss accounting platform for invoices, time tracking, projects, customers, proposals, and bookkeeping workflows.

authentication.name: Personal Access Token
authentication.description: Use a MILKEE personal access token. Requests send the token as a Bearer value in the Authorization header.

setupGuide.title: Get your MILKEE API token
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a MILKEE account with access to the company you want to connect. MILKEE shows a new API token only once, so keep it somewhere safe before leaving the screen.

steps.title: Open the MILKEE API area
steps.description: Sign in to MILKEE, then go to Integrationen -> API.

steps.title: Create a personal access token
steps.description: Choose Token erstellen, enter a clear description for the token, and create it.

steps.title: Copy the token immediately
steps.description: Copy the token before closing the page or dialog. MILKEE will not show the same token value again later.

steps.title: Find your company ID
steps.description: In MILKEE, choose the company from the left navigation, then go to Einstellungen -> Mein Unternehmen. Copy the value from the field "Firmen-ID fur API".

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Use a Zilliz Cloud API key with a cluster endpoint to access Milvus data-plane APIs.
authentication.notes: Supply a Zilliz Cloud API key that has access to the target cluster. Also provide the cluster endpoint host from the Zilliz Cloud console or Describe Cluster API; do not include https:// in that value.

setupGuide.title: Connect Milvus Vector Store with a Zilliz Cloud API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a running Zilliz Cloud cluster and an API key with access to that cluster.

steps.title: Copy a Zilliz Cloud API key
steps.description: In Zilliz Cloud, open API Keys and copy a key that can access the target project and cluster.

steps.title: Find the cluster endpoint host
steps.description: Open the target cluster in Zilliz Cloud and copy the endpoint host, or call Describe Cluster (V2) and copy the returned connect address. Paste only the host value and omit the https:// prefix.

steps.title: Enter both values in MindCloud
steps.description: Use the API key field for the bearer token and the Cluster Endpoint field for the cluster host. MindCloud will send requests to https://<cluster-endpoint>.

authentication.name: Access Key + Secret Key
authentication.description: Connect to MinIO using an access key, secret key, and MinIO endpoint URLs.
authentication.notes: MinIO uses S3-compatible request signing with an access key and secret key. Use sandbox credentials only for the public play cluster; treat all uploaded data there as public.

credentials.name: Secret Key

credentials.name: Console URL

setupGuide.title: Connect a MinIO deployment
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a MinIO access key, secret key, API endpoint URL, and console URL. For the public play cluster, uploaded data should be treated as public.

steps.title: Enter the Base API URL
steps.description: Use the HTTPS S3-compatible endpoint, for example https://play.min.io:9000.

steps.title: Enter the Console URL
steps.description: Use the human-facing console origin, for example https://play.min.io.

steps.title: Save and test the connection
steps.description: MindCloud will use these values to run S3-compatible bucket and object actions.

name: Mixpanel
description: Analyze product usage, manage cohorts, and export analytics data

authentication.name: Service Account
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Mixpanel service account username and secret.

credentials.name: Region And Domain
credentials.description: Mixpanel API host token used in docs as {regionAndDomain}.com.

setupGuide.title: Connect Mixpanel service account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Mixpanel service account username and secret with access to the Mixpanel project you want to use.

steps.title: Confirm you have service account credentials
steps.description: Mixpanel recommends Service Accounts for most authenticated APIs. If you do not already have a service account username and secret, ask a Mixpanel admin or owner to create one and grant it access to the target project.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: In the Mixpanel connection form, paste the service account username into the username field and the service account secret into the password field.

steps.title: Save and test the connection
steps.description: Save the connection, then run a safe read action such as List Annotations with a project ID that the service account can access.

authentication.name: Project Secret
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Mixpanel project secret using HTTP Basic auth.

credentials.name: Region And Domain
credentials.description: Mixpanel API host token used in docs as {regionAndDomain}.com.

setupGuide.title: Connect Mixpanel project secret
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the Mixpanel project secret for the project you want to access. Mixpanel marks project-secret auth as deprecated and recommends service accounts for most new work.

steps.title: Find the project secret in Mixpanel
steps.description: Open the target Mixpanel project and locate Project Settings, then Access Keys, and copy the Project Secret value.

steps.title: Enter the secret in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the project secret into the API key field for the Mixpanel connection. Leave Region And Domain as the default `mixpanel` unless your Mixpanel workspace uses a different regional domain.

steps.title: Save and run the connection test action
steps.description: Save the connection and run Export Today's Events. That action does not require extra inputs and is the safest current validation path for a project secret on this workspace.

actions.name: Create Draft Campaign
actions.description: Creates a draft campaign in Moosend.

arguments.name: Campaign Type
arguments.description: You can set the campaign type to "Regular" or "Transactional".

arguments.name: Subject
arguments.description: The subject line of the campaign.

arguments.name: Sender Email
arguments.description: The email address of the campaign sender.

arguments.name: Reply To Email
arguments.description: The email address selected to receive replies from the campaign. This must be one of your campaign senders. If not specified, the SenderEmail is assumed.

arguments.name: Confirmation To Email
arguments.description: The email address used to send a confirmation message when the campaign has been successfully sent. This can be any valid email address. If not specified, the SenderEmail is assumed.

arguments.name: HTMLContent
arguments.description: The complete HTML body of the campaign. You can use this parameter instead of using the WebLocation parameter.

arguments.name: Web Location
arguments.description: The URL used to retrieve the HTML content of the campaign. Moosend automatically moves all CSS inline.

arguments.name: Mailing Lists
arguments.description: A list of email lists in your account that is used to send the campaign.

arguments.name: Segment ID
arguments.description: The ID of a segment in the selected email list. If not specified, the campaign is sent to all active subscribers of the email list.

arguments.name: Is AB
arguments.description: A flag that defines if a campaign is an A/B split campaign. If true , you must fill out A/B split campaign parameters .

arguments.name: Track In Google Analytics
arguments.description: Specifies if tracking is enabled for the campaign. You must have Google Analytics configured on your site to use this feature.

arguments.name: ABCampaign Type
arguments.description: Specify the type of test to be performed in the AB split campaign to determine the winning version: Subjectline - test two different versions of the subject line. Content - test two different versions of the campaign content. Sender - test two different versions of the campaign sender.

arguments.name: Subject B
arguments.description: If testing A/B split campaigns with two subject line versions, this is the second subject version of the subject.

arguments.name: HTMLContent B
arguments.description: If testing A/B split campaigns with two HTML content versions, this is the complete HTML body of the second version.

arguments.name: Web Location B
arguments.description: If testing A/B split campaigns with two HTML content versions, this is the web location of the second HTML content version.

arguments.name: Sender Email B
arguments.description: If testing A/B split campaigns with two sender versions, this is the email address of the second campaign sender. This must be one of the senders defined in your account.

arguments.name: Hours To Test
arguments.description: Specify how long the test runs, before determining the winning campaign version to be sent to the rest of the recipients. This must be an integer between 1 and 24.

arguments.name: List Percentage
arguments.description: Specifies a portion of the target recipients to get the test campaign versions. For example, if you specify 10, then 10% of your recipients receive campaign A and another 10% receive the campaign B version. This must be an integer between 5 and 40.

arguments.name: ABWinner Selection Type
arguments.description: Specifies the method to determine the winning version for the test. If not set, OpenRate is assumed. OpenRate - determine the winner based on the version that achieved more opens. TotalUniqueClicks - determine the winner based on the version that achieved more unique link clicks.

actions.name: Update Draft Campaign
actions.description: Updates a draft campaign in Moosend.

arguments.name: Campaign ID
arguments.description: The ID of the campaign that you want to update.

arguments.name: Subject
arguments.description: The subject line of the campaign.

arguments.name: Sender Email
arguments.description: The email address of the campaign sender.

arguments.name: Reply To Email
arguments.description: The email address selected to receive replies from the campaign. This must be one of your campaign senders. If not specified, the SenderEmail is assumed.

arguments.name: Confirmation To Email
arguments.description: The email address used to send a confirmation message when the campaign has been successfully sent. This can be any valid email address. If not specified, the SenderEmail is assumed.

arguments.name: HTMLContent
arguments.description: The full HTML content of the campaign. You can use this instead of WebLocation . Omitting this when updating a draft will remove the HTML content.

arguments.name: Web Location
arguments.description: The URL used to retrieve the HTML content of the campaign. Moosend automatically moves all CSS inline.

arguments.name: Mailing Lists
arguments.description: A list of email lists in your account that is used to send the campaign.

arguments.name: Segment ID
arguments.description: The ID of a segment in the selected email list. If not specified, the campaign is sent to all active subscribers of the email list.

arguments.name: Is AB
arguments.description: A flag that defines if a campaign is an A/B split campaign. If true , you must fill out A/B split campaign parameters.

arguments.name: Track In Google Analytics
arguments.description: Specifies if tracking is enabled for the campaign. You must have Google Analytics configured on your site to use this feature.

arguments.name: ABCampaign Type
arguments.description: Specify the type of test to be performed in the AB split campaign to determine the winning version: Subjectline - test two different versions of the subject line. Content - test two different versions of the campaign content. Sender - test two different versions of the campaign sender.

arguments.name: Subject B
arguments.description: If testing A/B split campaigns with two subject line versions, this is the second subject version of the subject.

arguments.name: Web Location B
arguments.description: If testing A/B split campaigns with two HTML content versions, this is the web location of the second HTML content version.

arguments.name: Sender Email B
arguments.description: If testing A/B split campaigns with two sender versions, this is the email address of the second campaign sender. This must be one of the senders defined in your account.

arguments.name: Hours To Test
arguments.description: Specify how long the test runs, before determining the winning campaign version to be sent to the rest of the recipients. This must be an integer between 1 and 24.

arguments.name: List Percentage
arguments.description: Specifies a portion of the target recipients to get the test campaign versions. For example, if you specify 10, then 10% of your recipients receive campaign A and another 10% receive the campaign B version. This must be an integer between 5 and 40.

arguments.name: ABWinner Selection Type
arguments.description: Specifies the method to determine the winning version for the test. If not set, OpenRate is assumed. OpenRate -determine the winner based on the version that achieved more opens. TotalUniqueClicks - determine the winner based on the version that achieved more unique link clicks.

actions.name: Update Segment
actions.description: Updates an existing segment in Moosend.

arguments.name: Mailing List ID
arguments.description: The ID of the email list that contains the segment.

arguments.name: Segment ID
arguments.description: The ID of the segment to be updated.

arguments.name: Name
arguments.description: The name of the segment. If not specified, the existing name is retained.

arguments.name: Match Type
arguments.description: Specifies how subscribers are returned by your segment based on matching criteria. If not specified, All is assumed. All (Default) - returns subscribers that match all the given criteria. Any - returns subscribers that match any of the given criteria.

arguments.name: Fetch Type
arguments.description: Specifies how many criteria-matching subscribers are contained in your segment. If not specified, All is assumed. All - returns all criteria matching subscribers. Top - returns only a maximum number of subscribers defined in  FetchValue . TopPercent - returns only a percentage of subscribers defined in  FetchValue .

arguments.name: Fetch Value
arguments.description: Specifies the maximum number for FetchType:Top or percentage for FetchType:TopPercent of members to be contained in the created segment. If not specified, 0 is assumed.

arguments.name: Criteria
arguments.description: An array containing the criteria parameters used to filter the email list. If not specified, existing criteria are retained. Field - the criterion used to filter the email list. See Field values . Comparer - the operator that defines how to compare a Field with its Value . See Comparer values . Value - the search term used to filter the specified Field . LastXMinutes - constrains the results by the time that has elapsed. DateFrom to DateTo - constrains the results by a date span. Date Function - the value used with custom fields of dateTime data type. See DateFunction values .

name: Moxie
description: Manage clients, projects, invoices, and payments

setupGuide.title: Connect your Moxie API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to your Moxie workspace settings and the Custom Integration feature enabled.

steps.title: Open Integrations in Moxie
steps.description: In your Moxie workspace, go to Workspace Settings > Connected Apps > Integrations.

steps.title: Enable Custom Integration
steps.description: Click Enable for Custom Integrations so Moxie creates your API profile, Base Endpoint URL, API key, and webhook settings.

steps.title: Copy your Base Endpoint URL
steps.description: Copy the Base Endpoint URL shown by Moxie. It should match your workspace pod, such as https://pod01.withmoxie.com/api/public.

steps.title: Copy your API key
steps.description: Copy the API key shown in the Custom Integration area and paste it into the MindCloud connection.

authentication.name: OAuth 2.0
authentication.description: Connect with a Microsoft work or school account to access SharePoint through Microsoft Graph.
authentication.notes: Use delegated Microsoft Graph permissions with a Microsoft 365 work or school account. Tenant admin consent may be required for Files.ReadWrite.All and Sites.ReadWrite.All.
authentication.scopes: offline_access User.Read Files.Read.All Files.ReadWrite.All Sites.Read.All Sites.ReadWrite.All

setupGuide.title: Connect MS SharePoint
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Microsoft 365 work or school tenant and permission to create or edit a Microsoft Entra app registration. Personal Microsoft accounts are not enough for the SharePoint APIs used in this connector.

steps.title: Register or reuse a Microsoft Entra application
steps.description: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open App registrations and create a new application, or reuse an existing MindCloud application if your team already manages one.

steps.title: Choose organization-only sign-in
steps.description: Under Supported account types, choose Accounts in any organizational directory. Do not choose an option that includes personal Microsoft accounts for this SharePoint connector.

steps.title: Add the MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: Open Authentication, add a Web platform, and register this redirect URI: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/mSSharePoint/callback

steps.title: Create a client secret
steps.description: Open Certificates & secrets, create a new client secret, and copy the secret Value immediately. Microsoft only shows the value once.

steps.title: Add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions
steps.description: Open API permissions, add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions, and include offline_access, User.Read, Files.Read.All, Files.ReadWrite.All, Sites.Read.All, and Sites.ReadWrite.All. Grant admin consent if your tenant requires it.

steps.title: Finish the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Provide the Application (client) ID and client secret value to the MindCloud team so the app-level OAuth settings can be completed, then sign in with a work or school account that already has access to the target SharePoint sites.

setupGuide.title: Connect Myphoner with an API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Myphoner admin account with API access enabled and your workspace subdomain.

steps.title: Open the API key page in Myphoner
steps.description: Sign in to Myphoner, then go to Manage > Integrations/API. Only admins can create account-wide API keys.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key for MindCloud
steps.description: Generate a dedicated account-wide API key for this integration or copy an existing one that is reserved for MindCloud.

steps.title: Find your workspace subdomain
steps.description: Use only the subdomain part of your Myphoner URL. For example, if your account URL is https://mindcloudapps0327.myphoner.com, enter mindcloudapps0327.

steps.title: Confirm your Myphoner plan includes API access
steps.description: This tenant currently returns 'Please upgrade your account to gain API access.' when calling /api/v2/lists, so API access must be enabled on the account before connection tests can succeed.

name: MySQL
description: Store data, run queries, build applications, and scale databases.

setupGuide.title: Set up your MySQL connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the MySQL host name, database name, username, and password for the database account MindCloud should use. If the server is remote, make sure it accepts TCP/IP connections from your allowed network path.

steps.title: Collect the MySQL connection details
steps.description: Get the Host, Database, User, and Password values for the MySQL database you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Choose the port
steps.description: If your administrator did not provide a custom port, use the standard MySQL TCP port 3306.

steps.title: Enter the connection fields in MindCloud
steps.description: In the MindCloud MySQL connection form, enter the Host, Port, Database, User, Password, Timeout, and Use ODBC values that match your MySQL environment.

name: Mythic Text
description: Transform Markdown into polished HTML and channel-specific output for Gmail, Google Docs, WordPress, web pages, and branded content workflows.

authentication.description: Authenticate Mythic Text by sending your API key in the X-API-Key header.

credentials.name: API Key

setupGuide.title: Connect Mythic Text with an API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Mythic Text API key from the Mythic Text dashboard or beta access flow.

steps.title: Open the Mythic Text API key page
steps.description: Go to the Mythic Text dashboard or API key page from the Mythic Text documentation site.

steps.title: Generate or copy your API key
steps.description: Create a new key if needed, or copy your existing key. Treat it like a secret because it grants API access.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the Mythic Text connection form in MindCloud and paste the value into the API Key field.

steps.title: Run Test Connection
steps.description: Use the built-in Test Connection action after saving the key so MindCloud can confirm the credential works against the live Mythic Text API.

name: myUplink
description: Control and monitor myUplink-connected heating and indoor climate systems through the myUplink public API.

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect with OAuth2 authorization code to access the user's myUplink systems and devices.
authentication.notes: Register a client in the myUplink developer portal. The redirect_uri used in authorization and token exchange must match the callback URL registered with myUplink. Access tokens last 3600 seconds; refresh tokens rotate and the previous refresh token is one-time use.

setupGuide.title: Connect myUplink
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a myUplink developer account and a registered myUplink API client. Keep the client secret private.

steps.title: Open the myUplink developer portal
steps.description: Sign in at the myUplink developer site, then open your application/client list.

steps.title: Create or open an API client
steps.description: Create a client for this MindCloud connection, or open an existing client you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Set the callback URL
steps.description: Copy the MindCloud OAuth callback URL from the connection screen and paste it into the myUplink client callback URL field.

steps.title: Enable API scopes
steps.description: Enable the documented READSYSTEM scope. Enable WRITESYSTEM too if you want actions that change smart home modes, device points, or zone settings.

steps.title: Enter the client credentials
steps.description: Use the client ID and client secret from myUplink when completing this MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Authorize your myUplink account
steps.description: Continue through the myUplink OAuth window and approve access for the account that owns the systems and devices you want to use.

actions.name: Get My Systems
actions.description: Retrieves systems for the authenticated myUplink user.

actions.description: Tests public API availability in myUplink.
